messages:
maya: Onboarding goliath70k (int3). Quick heads up — streaming long prompts with eviction=48k is producing token corruption midstream. Looks like stale KV pages replaying after the eviction boundary. Logs below.

maya: Repro command:
```bash
./run_inference --model goliath70k-int3 --streaming true --eviction 49152 --prompt-file long_prompt.txt
```

maya: Short diff from a failing run (expected vs produced, truncated):
```
expected: ... 76 112 54 300 19 2 199 ...
actual:   ... 76 112 54 300 19 2 76 112 ...  <-- repeats earlier tokens starting at ~49.2k
```

devin: Can you paste the minimal prompt (or a short wrapper) so I can try locally?

maya: minimal prompt is a 50k token sequence of repeating anchor lines — attaching gist link: https://gist.github.com/redwood/goliath-repro-49k

song: hmm. Eviction 49,152 = 48k boundary. Could be RoPE wrap/scale mismatch for the model's longer positional base. goliath's RoPE config uses extended base multipliers.

kate: I reproduced on my laptop with int4 too, but only when streaming + eviction interact. If I disable streaming or increase eviction to 64k the corruption disappears.

devin: So it's an interaction: streaming chunking + eviction kernel path + quantized memcpy? Any kernel differences for int3 path?

maya: Model config snippet:
```
positional_encoding: "rotary"
rope_base: 10000.0
max_position_embeddings: 70000
quant: int3
kv_layout: sharded
```

ci-bot: run/longctx-canonical-repro #42 started by maya

song: Hypothesis: during eviction we memcpy KV shards using an int3-optimized memcpy that truncates pointer offsets, causing the phase index applied to the restored page to be off by a small rotation. Over long positions that becomes token-repeat/ghosting.

devin: Try forcing higher-precision RoPE calculation at runtime: add --ropecalc=double and re-run the reproduce. If that clears, it's floating point/quant mismatch.

maya: Ran with --ropecalc=double. Streaming+eviction -> pass. No repeats in 5/5 runs.

kate: That sounds like a numeric precision/quantization interaction. Could also be a bug in the int3 kernel's prefetch/align on the eviction memcpy path.

song: Quick mitigations:
- Route long-context + streaming requests to int4 variant until kernel fix.
- Add a canary that disables eviction for streaming requests >48k.

devin: For triage: can you run the reproducer with env KVCACHE_SAFE_MEMCPY=1? That will use the fallback memcpy path and indicate whether it's a memcpy alignment issue.

maya: Set KVCACHE_SAFE_MEMCPY=1 and re-ran. Drift reduced but one out of 200 runs still shows a 2-token slip at ~64k.

devin: Ok. That suggests multiple contributing factors (memcpy alignment + numeric precision). Double-check the int3 packing/unpacking when we apply rotary matrices — small rounding on phase term might flip argmax after many steps.

song: I'll add a runtime guard in router: if model==goliath70k and streaming==true and context>48000 -> route to goliath70k-int4. Quick PR incoming.

kate: Also adding a unit test in eng-runtime to run the exact repro (small synthetic anchor) under int3 kernels with eviction enabled to fail fast in CI.

maya: I'll open an issue with a minimal reproducer script, attach logs, and tag eng-ml + eng-runtime. For now we'll hold long-streaming traffic on int3 variant.

opsbot: Created issue #ML-3217: "goliath70k int3: streaming + eviction -> KV replay/ghosting" assigned to @song.

maya: Thanks. Will follow up with the canary rollout plan. :thumbsup:

devin: Long term: kernel authoring team needs to audit int3 memcpy/alignment code and RoPE precision path. Also consider adding an ephemeral double-precision RoPE pass for eviction/restore to avoid phase drift.

maya: Agreed. I'll include the --ropecalc=double test in the issue as a regression-check step.

kate: FYI - telemetry shows ~0.9% of long requests use streaming+eviction combos for this model in prod, so routing is low risk.

song: PR #5123 opened to add route rule and CI test. Tagging for review.

maya: Closing loop — will post when PR is live and the canary is running.

maya: cc @eng-ml @eng-runtime
